android_mechanism: All list-row content (drawables/previews) eagerly prepared instead of only bound/visible rows
bug_description: The article list view renders store.articles through a Scroll container holding a Column with a plain ForEach, which is never virtualised; the card grid also uses a non-caching ForEach. Opening a feed or scrolling loads pages of articles (limit grows with 'load more'), and every accumulated article row/card — including off-screen ones — is built eagerly, with per-card context menus bound, slowing list display and paging in large feeds.
fix_summary: Both the list and grid render via LazyForEach over an IDataSource kept in sync with the store, so rows are created on demand as they enter the viewport.

test_oracle.definition: raw-instruction-retired sample count attributed to the app process during the measured step, aggregated from perf.data (HapRay perf.db instruction counts).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: 4.87G vs 344M instructions (14.2x); task clock 1569 vs 281 ms (5.6x); VmRSS +340MB vs +6MB (53x). Measured on Pura 70 Ultra, 600-article feed, 3 runs each (measurements-staging/sheafreader_article_list_foreach).

mechanism_oracle.definition: Count of article card component builds during open + load-more + scroll (ace trace), first-render latency after open, and dropped frames while scrolling.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed builds every accumulated article (hundreds) eagerly; fixed builds only viewport rows. unfixed first-render and scroll jank measurably worse.

reproduction: git -C hosts/sheafreader checkout case/sheafreader_article_list_foreach/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/sheafreader checkout case/sheafreader_article_list_foreach/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
